Undersökningen baseras på 1031 onlineintervjuer med personer 18-84 år under perioden 12-16 januari 2026. 40 procent svarar att de är mycket negativa och 25 procent att de är ganska negativa till böcker som skrivits helt eller delvis med hjälp av AI-verktyg. Drygt 3 procent är positiva, varav enbart 0,6 procent är mycket positiva. 14 procent svarade att de är osäkra och 18 procent att de inte har någon åsikt i frågan. Inställningen till frågan uppges vara marginell när det kommer till variabler som kön, ålder och utbildningsnivå. Med undantag att unga vuxna (18-29 år) är både klart mer negativa (72 procent) och mer positiva (5 procent, varav 1,4 procent är mycket positiva). Flera av de svarande som var negativa till böcker som skrivits helt eller delvis med hjälp av AI-verktyg uppger att det är viktigt för dem att veta att det finns en mänsklig röst bakom texten. Andra skäl är att de vill vara lojala med författarna som yrkeskår och att de upplever att AI-skriven litteratur håller låg kvalitet.

I want to discuss accessibility because it is the most important thing for making websites. Other A List Apart articles give you innovation and insight. This article will give you homework. These are just my personal views, but they’re pretty good. I want to start off with a couple of statements, and you will agree:
Designers are good people. entry.title: Stop New York’s Surveillance and Censorship Mandate Before It’s Too Late
entry.summary:
New York’s state budget could pass within days. Buried deep in the text is a provision that has nothing to do with balancing the books. Part C of the budget bill would require every 3D printer sold in New York to run surveillance software that scans every design file you create, and blocks anything an algorithm flags as a potential firearm component. A separate provision would expose researchers, journalists, and educators to felony charges simply for possessing or sharing certain design files.

This isn’t a niche issue for hobbyists. This is the state mandating censorship infrastructure on your devices, and handing printer companies a way to lock in and surveil users. It’s a direct attack on grassroots innovation and user control.

New York is one of the largest consumer markets in the country. When it mandates technology in hardware, manufacturers don’t build a New York-only version. They build one version and sell it everywhere. What passes in Albany won’t stay in New York.

The vote could happen within days. If you’re a New Yorker, contact your legislators now.

There are no excuses for any Member of Congress to support a clean reauthorization of Section 702. Anyone who votes to do so does not take your privacy seriously. Full stop.

Sold to the public as a foreign surveillance tool, it has become a backdoor for law enforcement to search through Americans’ private communications without ever obtaining a warrant. We need to act now to prevent Congress from reauthorizing 702 in a way that ignores the truth: This authority needs to change.

House Speaker Mike Johnson has confirmed that “the plan is to move a clean extension of FISA… for at least 18 months.” Our demands are common sense: no renewal without real reforms. A simple extension is a betrayal of every US resident who expects their government to respect their rights and the Constitution.

Your representative needs to hear from you right now, before the April 20 deadline. Contact them today.
